acceptance: Every shard artifact from a real canary run contains a JUnit XML file with per-test durations.
Setup time and test time per shard are recoverable from the run (step timings or a small summary field).
Workflow contract tests assert the JUnit output path and that the marker expression, shard count, and aggregation are unchanged.
context:
PR #2340 open against develop: branch fix/canary-junit-durations, commit 4067f2dceb39 (rebased onto 90a76a336). All CI green including ci-required-result; mergeStateStatus CLEAN; auto-merge withheld per closeout policy.

make pr-preflight green at that head, from the run's own log: focused fast lane 31594 passed / 22 skipped / 4 subtests passed (132.87s); required stage ci-lint and spellcheck passed; medium tier 2120 passed / 21 skipped (321.09s). Ordered wrapper returned ordered_success exit 0, with local-focused-check and required-pr-preflight receipts both bound to head 4067f2dceb39; a later re-check reused both receipts rather than re-executing.

Workflow contract tests assert the JUnit output path, the timing fields, and that the marker expression, shard count, --maxfail, and the release-canary-result aggregation are unchanged. Both shard branches were simulated locally against the YAML-extracted run scripts (empty shard -> fallback report marked junit_captured=false; populated shard -> real JUnit), and the emitted summary JSON parses with the marker expression intact. release_canary_incident.py globs only shard-*-pytest.log, so the new XML files cannot affect the incident job.

Two operational notes for whoever resumes here.

1. BENCHBOX_TEST_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS matches VALIDATION_ENV_PREFIXES (BENCHBOX_), so changing its value between runs forks the receipt identity and forces a full re-execution instead of reusing a valid green receipt. Use one value per branch. Set it positive at all, though: the pytest lock default is fail-fast, so a concurrent run in another worktree otherwise aborts the fast lane immediately.

2. tests/integration/test_database_integration.py::test_database_resource_management asserts RSS growth < 50MB and is environment-sensitive: it passed in one full medium run and failed in another on this machine (62MB in isolation). This branch does not touch that file, and CI runs make test-medium on ubuntu-latest only, so it never gates a merge. Pre-existing, not a regression from this branch; worth its own flake item.

Remaining acceptance item: confirm JUnit XML and setup/test timings actually appear in a real canary run's shard artifacts. That needs a live release-canary run after merge.

description:
The pre-merge canary-impact selector needs measured per-test durations to size shards and to estimate runner-minutes and wall time; selected-file counts alone cannot establish cost, because each shard also pays several minutes of setup and test runtimes vary widely. Today the canary shards write only a pytest text log.

Change: each release-canary.yml shard also writes a JUnit XML report (pytest --junitxml) into its existing uploaded artifact directory, and the run records per-shard setup time (checkout, uv sync) separately from test time.
